title: AI Agents and Tool Calling
description: Learn what agents are, how tool calling extends LLM capabilities, and how these concepts map to C# backends.

blocks.text: An AI agent is a system that uses an LLM to decide which actions to take, when to use tools, and how to combine their results. Tool calling is the mechanism by which the model requests execution of a structured function, such as querying a database, calling an API, or running C# code.

blocks.title: Key agent vocabulary
items: **Agent** — the overall system that plans, acts, observes, and repeats until the task is complete.
**Tool** — a structured function the agent can call, defined with a name, description, and typed parameters.
**Planner** — the reasoning step that decides which tool to call or whether to answer directly.
**Memory** — state carried across turns, such as conversation history or retrieved facts.
**Loop** — the repeated observe-plan-act cycle that gives agents multi-step behavior.

blocks.title: Conceptual tool definition in C#
blocks.content: The model sees this tool description and may request its execution.

blocks.title: Abstractions are shifting
blocks.text: Libraries are converging on common interfaces such as AIFunction. Prefer provider-agnostic interfaces so you can swap models or SDKs without rewriting tool logic.

items.text: I can explain the agent loop in one sentence
items.hint: Observe input, plan an action, call a tool, observe the result, repeat until done

items.text: I know what makes a good tool description
items.hint: Clear name, behavior description, typed parameters, and examples when helpful

items.text: I understand why agents need memory
items.hint: To remember prior tool results, corrections, and user preferences across turns

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Agents use LLMs to plan and call tools instead of following hardcoded workflows.
Tool calling turns backend logic into model-callable functions with typed inputs.
Memory and planning are the two parts that separate agents from simple single-turn APIs.
blocks.takeaway: Start with one well-defined tool and one clear task. Multi-tool agents are powerful, but correctness starts with simple, observable tool behavior.
